title: Ops health + econ pulse and roadmap alignment
topics: roadmap for canary rollouts and autoscale
summary: Quarterly pulse covering usage growth, recent cost surprise from a campaign, brief reliability incident post-deploy, and agreement on a small pilot to validate dedicated capacity + revised autoscale rules. Action items focus on benchmark run, security docs, and updated Node+Model mapping for cost forecasts.
action_items: Ravi Patel - run 1-hour simulated traffic benchmark with their 5k tps equivalent and share metrics by 2025-06-04
Maya Chen - send updated pricing worksheet and example cost scenarios for Hosted vs Dedicated by 2025-06-02
Lena Rodriguez - share top 10 prompts and sleeve of heavy endpoints for synthetic test by 2025-05-31
Jordan Lee - include SOC2/SSO/KMS one-pager and link to Private deployment checklist by 2025-06-03
next_steps: Schedule a 2-hour benchmarking session (AE/SE + customer infra) week of 2025-06-09
Customer to confirm pilot scope (traffic shape, success criteria) in Slack thread
Redwood to provision a canary Dedicated pool for pilot and provide runbook
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-29
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM) -- Lena Rodriguez (ThirdWave), Tom Brooks (ThirdWave CTO), Aisha Khan (ThirdWave Finance), Marcus Li (Infra)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight — agenda is usage & cost pulse, the little incident last week, and roadmap alignments for the pickup pilot. 
[00:18] Lena Rodriguez: Yep thanks, appreciate it. Quick note, Aisha will jump in on cost questions, Marcus on infra. 
[00:27] Tom Brooks: Sorry was on another call, joined. 
[00:34] Maya Chen: No worries Tom. Ravi, want to run the health summary? 
[00:38] Ravi Patel: Sure. So overall we've seen ThirdWave's token volume up about 78% month over month, which is great, but the cost per active session spiked on May 22 when the marketing campaign hit. The spike looks like longer sequences + repeated reranks; our prefix caching didn't catch a lot of the burst because many requests had unique user context. 
[01:05] Marcus Li: Yeah that was our end, a lot of cold KV cash — sorry KV cache — we had misses on the first 2K requests of the batch, and latency went from ~120ms p90 to about 950ms p90 for a 20-minute window. 
[01:26] Ravi Patel: Right, KV cache misses. Also, a couple of requests were routed to the smaller hosted variants because the Dedicated pool had momentary autoscale lag; we saw fallback to hosted which increased token unit costs unexpectedly. 
[01:43] Aisha Khan: To be clear, the invoice last week was ~42% higher than forecast. Finance is nervous. We need predictability. 
[01:53] Maya Chen: Totally get that. Our goal in this call is to propose a small pilot to validate a Dedicated pool with adjusted autoscale thresholds and a benchmark so we can demonstrate lower unit economics and stable latency. 
[02:07] Tom Brooks: Quick question — how much of that 42% is just from model size or is it from request shape? 
[02:14] Ravi Patel: Mostly request shape + repeated reranks. Model size contributed but not the primary driver. The reranking loop multiplied token usage; combined with cold cache it's the compound effect. 
[02:26] Lena Rodriguez: We can probably alter the client to keep more context on-device for some flows, but that's product work. Short term we'd like Redwood to help with an infra-level mitigation. 
[02:38] Jordan Lee: On the infra mitigation side we can do three things: one, run a targeted benchmark with your exact traffic traces; two, provision a dedicated pool with higher headroom and strict routing so requests don't fall back to hosted; three, tweak autoscale window and batch size. 
[02:58] Lena Rodriguez: Sounds good. How long to spin a dedicated pool for a pilot? 
[03:03] Maya Chen: We can provision a small canary Dedicated pool in about 48 hours; full sized tests take a couple days to stabilize because of kernel warmup and KV caching patterns. 
[03:15] Marcus Li: Important note — we are restricted on data residency and need audit logs for PCI scope. If we go Dedicated, we need KMS integration and an audit export. 
[03:27] Ravi Patel: Understood. For Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and we can push audit logs to your SIEM or S3 with retention controls. We'll include the Private checklist and SOC2 artifacts in the one-pager. 
[03:43] Aisha Khan: For pricing, can you show Hosted vs Dedicated line items? We need an apples-to-apples sample. 
[03:50] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send an updated pricing worksheet and three scenarios: steady-state, marketing burst, and aggressive rerank heavy. We'll annotate where caching helps. 
[04:05] Tom Brooks: On SLAs, what happens if the Dedicated pool has a deployment that increases latency for us? Are there fallback rules? 
[04:14] Ravi Patel: We offer three-tier fallbacks: prefer local pool, then compatible model variant in the same region, then hosted as last resort. For the pilot we'll lock to avoid fallback — the whole point is to measure Dedicated isolation. 
[04:28] Lena Rodriguez: Ok locking is good, but we still want an automatic temporary spill to a safe variant in case of total pool outage. We can't have total outage, but temporary spill is fine. 
[04:40] Maya Chen: We'll propose a 'soft-lock' canary policy: prefer Dedicated, block fallback for short bursts but allow controlled spill on full outage to a verified cheaper variant. We'll document the exact thresholds. 
[04:54] Marcus Li: Security — need SSO/SAML mapping to roles. We don't want everyone to get admin. 
[04:59] Jordan Lee: We support SAML + SCIM and RBAC; we'll share role templates. 
[05:06] Aisha Khan: Also need KMS key rotation policy and proof of separation for audit. 
[05:11] Ravi Patel: We'll include KMS rotation cadence docs and how keys are managed in both Redwood-managed and customer-managed flows. 
[05:19] Tom Brooks: Great. On the benchmark — what's the plan? 
[05:22] Ravi Patel: We ask ThirdWave to provide the top 10 heavy prompt shapes, approximate traffic mix, and a synthetic traffic script. We'll run the script against both Hosted (current config) and Dedicated (pilot config) for a 1 hour steady run and a 30 min burst run. Metrics: p50/p90 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens. 
[05:45] Lena Rodriguez: We can extract the prompts, but the example user contexts are sensitive. Can we run with anonymized context? 
[05:51] Ravi Patel: Yep anonymized is fine; we only need request shapes and length distributions. 
[05:56] Maya Chen: Quick logistics: Jordan will pack the SOC2/KMS/SSO one-pager. Ravi will run the benchmark. I'll send pricing and a pilot runbook. 
[06:08] Aisha Khan: Timeline question — how soon can we see numbers? Finance wants an estimate by next Friday. 
[06:14] Maya Chen: If Lena posts the prompt shapes by end of Sunday (05-31), Ravi can run the first benchmark early next week and we'll share preliminary numbers by 2025-06-04. 
[06:25] Tom Brooks: Also want a small list of risk triggers for autoscale and rollbacks. If we roll out model changes, we need fast rollback. 
[06:33] Ravi Patel: We'll include rollback playbook and suggested canary batch sizes; canary traffic should be <5% of total to start. 
[06:41] Lena Rodriguez: One more ask: can Redwood provide sample telemetry dashboards that align with our internal monitoring? We want token split by route and model to reconcile billing. 
[06:50] Jordan Lee: Yes we have token-level breakdowns and per-route latency charts; we'll share prebuilt dashboards for Grafana/Looker and a CSV export format. 
[07:02] Aisha Khan: On competitors, we were also evaluating Vertex but their pricing was opaque for multiple regions. Anthropic came up for safety reasons, but they didn't match our latency needs. Redwood's dev experience is strong. 
[07:14] Maya Chen: Appreciate the context. Anything else? 
[07:19] Marcus Li: Need to confirm network topology for Dedicated - public egress or VPC-only. We'll share our VPC peering constraints. 
[07:28] Maya Chen: We'll include the Private deployment checklist with VPC options. 
[07:33] Tom Brooks: Ok, that's it from me. Sounds like clear next steps. 
[07:38] Maya Chen: Great. Quick recap: Lena to share prompts & traffic shape by 2025-05-31; Ravi to run bench and share numbers by 2025-06-04; Jordan to send security one-pager by 2025-06-03; Maya to send pricing by 2025-06-02. We'll schedule a 2-hour bench session week of 2025-06-09. 
[07:58] Lena Rodriguez: Confirmed. Thanks everyone. 
[08:02] Maya Chen: Thanks, meeting adjourned.
